{"claims":[{"claim_text":"States will be free to deny mental health, reproductive services and other crucial medical services from minimal plan requirements.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"States will be able to shift individuals with prior health problems into unaffordable “high risk” insurance pools.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"High risk pools were tried by 35 states before the ACA and almost all failed because of state underfunding.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"DSA argued that the ACA inefficiently expanded health insurance coverage by providing a huge federal subsidy to the private health care industry.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"DSA supported expanding Medicaid coverage to nearly 13 million working people and their children.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Another ten million would be added to Medicaid coverage if the remaining 19 Republican states took the federal funds for Medicaid expansion.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Republican bill will begin to cut Medicaid coverage immediately after the 2020 presidential election.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The Republican bill will eliminate Medicaid coverage entirely by 2023.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
